title: The component locus of a section is locally constructible
statement: Let g:P→T be a locally finitely presented, quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let σ:T→P satisfy σ≫g=id_T. The subset C={p∈P | p lies in the connected component of σ(g(p)) in the subspace g⁻¹({g(p)})} is locally constructible: every point of P has an open neighbourhood U on which C∩U is constructible.

proof.text: Use the local noetherian model theorem to choose an open neighbourhood whose component locus is the inverse image of a component locus for a noetherian morphism.

For the noetherian model, apply noetherian induction on closed subsets. The generic dichotomy theorem supplies an open trace on each irreducible closed set; the induction and finite union argument make the component locus constructible.
Constructibility is preserved by inverse image along the projection, so the chosen neighbourhood witnesses local constructibility.
